steps.message:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Ulakwo, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 14.369 | 0.124 | 0.12415
2 | 15.965 | 8.25 | 9.665
3 | 4591.4 | 27.074 | 47.738
4 | 5101.5 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as HA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Ulakwo, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Groundwater Site Note: Station Ulakwo (Etche LGA)**

**Layer Sequence Summary:**
- **Layer 1:** 14.37 Ωm, thickness 0.12 m (depth: 0.12 m)
- **Layer 2:** 15.97 Ωm, thickness 8.25 m (depth: 9.67 m)
- **Layer 3:** 4591.40 Ωm, thickness 27.07 m (depth: 47.74 m)
- **Layer 4:** 5101.50 Ωm, basement/sub-stratum

**Curve Type Analysis:**
Resistivity values increase monotonically with depth ($r_1 < r_2 < r_3 < r_4$). The sequence yields an A-type configuration for layers 1–3 ($14.37 < 15.97 < 4591.40\text{ }\Omega\text{m}$) and an A-type configuration for layers 2–4 ($15.97 < 4591.40 < 5101.50\text{ }\Omega\text{m}$), resulting in an **AA** (or **A**) curve type. The HA classification on file is inconsistent with the data because $r_1 < r_2$, whereas an H-segment requires $r_1 > r_2 < r_3$.
